narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job. In this promotion process, that high retention risk is why you were denied a promotion: the organization is treating likely departure as a reason not to invest in advancing you now.

The strongest driver was your overall work experience. You have six to ten years of experience, compared with the most common stayer profile of one to five years, and this made leaving look more likely. The second driver was that you have other job opportunities while in this role; most employees predicted to stay—about three in four—report no such outside opportunities, so this strongly increased the leaving signal. The third driver was your one-to-five years in your current organization. Although this tenure is common among stayers, in your profile it also leaned toward leaving.

This does not mean the decision is permanent or that your performance is unimportant. You report job satisfaction, recognition and high emotional commitment, which are positive. The organization should hold a retention conversation with you, clarify the promotion path and timeline, and address job stability and development needs. You should also communicate whether you intend to stay and what support or opportunities would keep you engaged.
